## Series Analysis Complete — ³¹P VT-NMR (Mg(OTf)₂/TEP electrolyte)

Analyzed all 5 spectra as one temperature series (243.2 → 313.2 K), correctly mapping each alphabetically-sorted filename to its temperature. All ³¹P signals fall in the **−6 to −2.8 ppm** window, consistent with organophosphate (TEP) phosphorus.

**Key trends vs temperature:**

| Observable | Trend (243→313 K) | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| **Linewidth (FWHM)** | 702 → 39 Hz (strong narrowing) | Reduced viscosity (faster tumbling, longer T2*) ± motional averaging of exchange |
| **Main peak position** | −3.6 → −2.8 ppm (toward less negative) | T-dependent shift of the averaged resonance |
| **Component count** | 2 sites at 243/258 K → 1 averaged line at higher T | Possible slow→fast chemical exchange (coalescence) |

**Two-site regime (cold points only):**
- Sharp component near **−6 / −5.6 ppm**, population ~0.10 → 0.073
- Broad component near **−3.2 ppm** carrying ~90% of the integral

**Scientific reading:** The behavior is consistent with a **slow-to-fast chemical-exchange (coalescence) scenario** for TEP speciation — e.g., Mg-coordinated vs. free/bulk TEP — resolved into two environments only at the two coldest temperatures, collapsing to a single motionally-averaged line as T rises.

**Caveats (honest):**
- The two-site regime is defined by **only two low-T points**, and the component count was manually locked — so exchange is *plausible but not proven*; viscosity broadening alone could reproduce the FWHM trend.

- The **30 T1 relaxation curves** in the campaign were *not* integrated here — they could disambiguate relaxation vs. exchange contributions to the linewidth.
